The test makes two direct calls to `Stack.configure`. In the first call, the outsider window is not in any of the three stacks, so the `for` loop checks each stack, falls through the `else`, then hides the client and returns. In the second call, `w5` is found in the third stack, so the loop breaks on that stack; because `w5.has_focus` is false and `border_normal_stack` is set while that stack is split, the code chooses the non-focus split border path, then computes column/window geometry, takes the `s.split` branch, calls `place`, and finally `unhide`.
